name: Illinois
note: The funeral director who first takes custody reports to the local registrar within 24 hours and files the death certificate within seven days, through the State Registrar's electronic system. The treating health care professional, or the coroner or medical examiner in reportable cases, certifies the cause within 48 hours. The electronic system must update the Medicaid roster at least quarterly, and vital records officers report adult deaths monthly to boards of election commissioners. Certified copies are restricted to people with a personal or property right interest.

steps.title: Notify the coroner of a death subject to investigation
steps.who: Every law enforcement official, funeral director, ambulance attendant, hospital director or administrator, person having custody of the body, and any physician in attendance.
steps.trigger: A sudden or violent death, a death in suspicious or unexplained circumstances, one where addiction may have contributed, or one not attended by a licensed physician.
steps.summary: Failing to notify the coroner promptly is a Class A misdemeanour. The coroner (or medical examiner in Cook County) goes to the body, takes charge of it and makes a preliminary investigation; this is also the closest Illinois law comes to an official pronouncement for unattended deaths.

steps.title: Certifying health care professional signs the medical certification
steps.who: The health care professional who was treating the illness that caused death within the preceding 12 months, or an associate physician, APRN or PA, the institution's chief medical officer, or the autopsy physician.
steps.trigger: The funeral director presents the certificate.
steps.summary: The medical certification is completed within 48 hours of death, except in coroner cases.

steps.title: Coroner or medical examiner completes the certificate of death
steps.who: The county coroner or medical examiner.
steps.trigger: A death without medical attendance or otherwise subject to investigation.

deadline.text: within 48 hours after death, except special problem cases

steps.summary: The coroner or medical examiner completes a coroner's or medical examiner's certificate of death and signs the medical certification within 48 hours.

steps.title: Funeral director's 24-hour report to the registrar, which serves as the burial permit
steps.who: The funeral director or person acting as such who first assumes custody of the body.

deadline.text: within 24 hours after taking custody of the body

steps.summary: The funeral director's written report doubles as the permit to transport and bury within Illinois, provided the certifier has agreed to sign. It does not authorise cremation, removal from the state, or disposal in coroner cases, which need a full permit.

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate with the local registrar
steps.who: The funeral director who first assumes custody of the body, using personal data from the next of kin or the best qualified source.

deadline.text: within 7 days after death and before cremation or removal from the State

steps.summary: The certificate is filed with the local registrar of the district of death, through the State Registrar's electronic death registration system. Willful neglect of a duty under the Act is a Class A misdemeanour; false statements are a Class 4 felony.

steps.title: Local registrar issues the permit for disposition
steps.who: The registrar of the district where death occurred or the body was found.
steps.trigger: Filing of a properly completed death certificate; required before cremation, removal from the State, or disposal in a coroner case.
steps.summary: No permit for disposition may issue until a properly completed certificate has been filed.

steps.title: Copy sent to the registrar of the decedent's county of residence
steps.who: The local registrar where the certificate was filed.
steps.trigger: Filing of a certificate for a death outside the decedent's county of residence.
steps.summary: When someone dies outside their home county, the filing registrar sends a copy to the registrar of the county of residence.

steps.title: Funeral director reports a veteran's burial to the Illinois Department of Veterans' Affairs
steps.who: The funeral director, to the Illinois Department of Veterans' Affairs.
steps.trigger: Death of a veteran of any US war.
steps.summary: The funeral director prepares a Certificate of Burial of U.S. War Veteran and submits it monthly.

steps.title: Electronic death registration system updates the Medicaid roster
steps.who: The State Registrar's electronic reporting system, to the Department of Healthcare and Family Services.

deadline.text: not less often than once every 3 months

steps.summary: The system must transfer death information to HFS at least quarterly to update the roster of Medicaid recipients.

steps.title: State Registrar marks the birth record deceased and tells the local custodian
steps.who: The State Registrar, to the municipal or county custodian of the birth record.
steps.trigger: Receipt or preparation of a death certificate.
steps.summary: The birth record is annotated as deceased and the local custodian annotates its copy; copies then issue stamped "DECEASED" only on an identifying request form.

steps.title: Requests for a deceased person's birth certificate are sent to HFS and DHS for a benefits check
steps.who: The State Registrar, to the Department of Healthcare and Family Services and the Department of Human Services.
steps.trigger: A request for the birth certificate of a deceased person.

deadline.text: no later than 60 days after receipt of the request form

steps.summary: HFS and DHS must check that no public-assistance claim is being made by or for the deceased person.

steps.title: Vital records officer reports adult deaths monthly to the board of election commissioners
steps.who: The person or officer in charge of a city, village or town's vital records, to its board of election commissioners.
steps.trigger: Deaths of persons over 18 in the preceding month.
steps.summary: The board of election commissioners must then strike the deceased from the precinct registers.

steps.title: County clerk may erase deceased voters using the clerk's own death records
steps.who: The county clerk (in counties under Article 4 of the Election Code), who also holds death records.
steps.trigger: Death records on file in the clerk's office.
steps.summary: The clerk may treat information from its death records as an application to erase the name from the register, after notice.

steps.title: Death data furnished for national statistics
steps.who: The State Registrar, to the National Vital Statistics Division or its successor (and to other agencies for statistical purposes).
steps.trigger: Request; the State is reimbursed for the cost.
steps.summary: Data may be furnished for national statistics and may not be used for other purposes without the State Registrar's authorisation.

steps.title: Certified copies issued to persons with a personal or property right interest
steps.who: The State Registrar, local registrars and county clerks (who may issue certifications from the electronic system).
steps.summary: Access to vital records is closed except as the Act allows. A certified copy of a death certificate goes to a person (or agent) with a genealogical, personal or property right interest, to the estate's administrator or executor, to government departments, or by court order; genealogical requests are limited to deaths at least 20 years old and stamped accordingly.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Within 7 days after death and before cremation or removal from the State, except coroner/medical examiner cases.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director who first assumes custody files; next of kin supply the personal data.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No review of every certificate; the coroner or medical examiner certifies only deaths subject to investigation, though cremation requires a registrar's permit rather than the 24-hour report.

electronicRegistration.note: The State Registrar must run an electronic reporting system for death registrations; county clerks issue certifications from it.

governmentPropagation.note: State law requires a quarterly death feed to the Medicaid roster and monthly death reports to boards of election commissioners; other agencies are told separately. SSA feeds are in the federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: Only persons with a genealogical (deaths 20+ years old), personal or property right interest, the estate's representative, government, or by court order.

gaps: No Illinois statute found authorising nurses or other non-physicians to pronounce death; the Nurse Practice Act (225 ILCS 65) was not searched.
No state-law provision found requiring the Secretary of State to cancel a driver's licence or the Department of Revenue to be notified on a death report (625 ILCS 5/6-201 does not mention death).

Election Code: only the board-of-election-commissioner route (10 ILCS 5/6-62, 6-63) and the county clerk's discretionary use of its own death records (4-16) were found; no statewide IDPH-to-State Board of Elections feed was located in the sections read.
The State Registrar's electronic feed to SSA is not in the Vital Records Act; it is left to the us-federal layer.
privateSectorVerification is deliberately omitted so the us-federal value (LADMF) applies; Illinois law only lets persons with a property right interest obtain copies.

www.ilga.gov serves an incomplete certificate chain; it was read by adding the Sectigo OV R40 intermediate fetched from the leaf's AIA URL (crt.sectigo.com) to the trust store, with verification left on.
